set.body:
Split out of P8.A5, which closed four of six holes. These two remain.

1. DurableResultHandle and TaskInvocation still have public apply/copy.
core/StructuredResult.scala:29-41 and :43-57. Unlike ResultContractDescriptor (closed in A5, zero callers outside core), these are constructed in THREE modules each:
  - DurableResultHandle: managed/ResultAttachment.scala, protocol/StructuredResultCodec.scala, worker/RegisteredTaskLauncher.scala
  - TaskInvocation: protocol/StructuredResultCodec.scala, worker/RegisteredTaskLauncher.scala, worker/TaskRuntime.scala
Closing them means a validating `from` plus threading Either through six call sites, several of which are decoders. That is the RIGHT place for it — decoding is exactly where parse-don't-validate applies, and the decoders already return Either — but it is a real refactor rather than a one-line closure, and A5 was already carrying five other changes.

Invariants to enforce when done:
  - declaredOutputs distinct (both)
  - maximumResultBytes <= maximumEnvelopeBytes (both)
  - inputBytes.size <= maximumInputBytes (TaskInvocation)
The bounded-envelope guarantees ADR 0001 claims are exactly these, and today nothing enforces them on a value arriving from the wire.

2. SiteToken is one type for account, partition, QoS, constraints, modules, container and accelerator kind.
core/SiteProfile.scala:7-11, 29, 47-57, 89-101, 113. An account and a partition are freely interchangeable at the type level; SiteProfile.resolve (:170-172) only guards when an allowlist is configured. A5 explicitly ranked this last and said not to let it block the other five.

Sequencing note: both overlap P8.D2 (PreparedJob/PreparedAttempt), which reshapes the durable result plan. Doing item 1 immediately before D2 avoids writing the smart constructors twice — or fold it into D2.
set.title: P8.A5b: Close DurableResultHandle, TaskInvocation, and SiteToken construction
